plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This holds because your payment depends only on others' bids, not your own bid, so shading up or down only risks losing profitable wins or winning at a loss. With a value of $26, the optimal action is to bid exactly $26, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay less than my value when I do win.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (given you win). Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying relative to value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds regardless of competitors' strategies, the optimal action is straightforward truthful bidding. My value is $31, so I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, truthful bidding (bidding exactly your value) is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since your bid only affects whether you win, not what you pay if you win. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
